item.title: Generative AI and Data Envelopment Analysis for Performance Measurement and Public Value
item.content:encoded:
This special issue explores the intersection of generative artificial intelligence and data envelopment analysis as tools for measuring organizational performance and creating public value. The collection seeks research that demonstrates how these technologies can enhance performance evaluation methodologies and provide insights into efficiency across various sectors, particularly in public organizations where value creation extends beyond traditional financial metrics.

Appel publié par Socio-Economic Planning Sciences. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Applications of generative AI in performance measurement
  • Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA) methodologies
  • Public value creation and assessment
  • Integration of AI and DEA techniques
  • Performance evaluation in public sector organizations
  • Efficiency measurement using advanced analytics

Timeline

  • September 1, 2026: Submission deadline

item.title: Gender diversity in the public sector: reforms, challenges, and emerging opportunities
item.content:encoded:
Younes Ben Zaied, EDC Paris Business School

Shajara Ul-Durar, University of Sunderland

Assil Guizani, EDC Paris Business School

Alessandro Marra, University d'Annunzio of Chieti-Pescara

This special issue examines how gender diversity influences governance and public service outcomes. While private sector research on gender diversity is extensive, its role in public administration and state-owned enterprises remains underexplored despite its significance for equitable and accountable governance. The call seeks contributions exploring how gender-diverse teams improve decision-making quality, reduce groupthink, and strengthen public sector performance.

Governments worldwide have implemented reforms to increase female representation in public institutions, including quota systems and legal mandates. However, significant implementation gaps persist, with uneven progress in developing talent pipelines and achieving executive-level representation. This special issue investigates the actual impact of these policies on organizational outcomes and identifies barriers and enablers of women's advancement in public organizations.

Appel publié par Public Money & Management. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Gender diversity and public sector performance
  • Women in state-owned enterprises
  • Public service delivery and gender-sensitive governance
  • Barriers and enablers of women's advancement in public organizations
  • Gender, ethics, and public integrity
  • Future directions: towards gender-responsive public management
  • Representative bureaucracy effects of women in executive agencies
  • The extent to which mentorship and sponsorship programs improve women's advancement
  • Gender differences in promotion rates in public agencies

Timeline

  • November 30, 2026: Submission deadline for research articles and new development pieces
  • January 1, 2027: Submission deadline for debate pieces
